react_result.final_narrative_text: Three independent enrichment paradigms converge on a single dominant pathway perturbation. RaMP multi-database ORA (FDR 8.86e-19), MetaboAnalystR KEGG-specific PSEA (p = 5.41e-09), and Mummichog m/z-direct network activity (p = 2.52e-04) all rank Tryptophan metabolism (KEGG:hsa00380 / KEGG:map00380 / MUMM:tryptophan_metabolism) as the top hit. Seven of the nine input metabolites are annotated members of the KEGG hsa00380 roster: L-Tryptophan (KEGG:C00078) as the pathway substrate, Quinolinic acid (KEGG:C03722) and 3-Hydroxyanthranilic acid (KEGG:C00632) representing the kynurenine branch, Serotonin (KEGG:C00780), Melatonin (KEGG:C01598), Tryptamine (KEGG:C00398), and Indoleacetaldehyde (KEGG:C00637) occupying the biogenic-amine and indole branches. The kynurenine arm is further confirmed by WP:WP5414 (IDO metabolic pathway, FDR 8.38e-09), which specifically captures 3-Hydroxyanthranilic acid, Quinolinic acid, and L-Tryptophan. The serotonergic arm is independently supported by REACT:R-HSA-209931 (Serotonin and melatonin biosynthesis, FDR 2.02e-08). N-Carbamoyl-L-aspartic acid (KEGG:C00438) and O-Phosphoethanolamine (KEGG:C00346) are peripheral hits: the former maps to pyrimidine metabolism (MetaboAnalystR rank 4, p = 0.180) and the latter to glycerophospholipid metabolism (Mummichog rank 3), consistent with ureidosuccinic acid's role in de novo pyrimidine synthesis. The biological story is a coordinated perturbation of tryptophan catabolism, with simultaneous enrichment across the neuroactive (serotonin-melatonin) and immunometabolic (kynurenine-NAD+) branches, implicating both neurotransmitter and redox/immune axes in the treatment mechanism.

RaMP-DB multi-database ORA (run_ramp_enrichment) returned KEGG:map00380 'Tryptophan metabolism' as the top hit with an FDR of 8.86e-19, driven by seven input compounds (L-tryptophan, serotonin, 3-hydroxyanthranilic acid, quinolinic acid, indoleacetaldehyde, tryptamine, and melatonin) out of 54 pathway members. RaMP-DB multi-database ORA (run_ramp_enrichment) returned KEGG:map00380 'Tryptophan metabolism' as the top hit with an FDR of 8.86e-19, driven by seven input compounds (L-tryptophan, serotonin, 3-hydroxyanthranilic acid, quinolinic acid, indoleacetaldehyde, tryptamine, and melatonin) out of 54 pathway members. WikiPathways WP:WP465 reported the same pathway at FDR 4.15e-15, while WP:WP4210 'Tryptophan catabolism leading to NAD+ production' was rank 4 (FDR 5.82e-11) and REACT:R-HSA-209931 'Serotonin and melatonin biosynthesis' was rank 7 (FDR 2.02e-08). MetaboAnalystR PSEA (run_metaboanalystr_psea) independently confirmed KEGG:hsa00380 (Tryptophan metabolism) with p = 5.41e-09, hitting six of the same metabolites. Mummichog m/z-direct analysis returned MUMM:tryptophan_metabolism as the top pathway (p = 0.000168) with 16 of 17 matched features, confirming network-coherent activity. The cross-paradigm consensus is strong: rank ≤ 1 across all four tools, with consistent compound rosters. Ureidosuccinic acid (KEGG:C00438) and O-phosphoethanolamine (KEGG:C00346) did not contribute to the tryptophan signal; mummichog placed them in separate lower-ranked hits (pyrimidine and glycerophospholipid metabolism, p > 0.04). L-Tryptophan (C00078) is the entry-point substrate; serotonin (C00780) and melatonin (C01598) represent the biogenic-amine branch, while 3-hydroxyanthranilic acid (C00632) and quinolinic acid (C03722) reflect kynurenine-pathway activation. The treatment therefore appears to co-stimulate both the serotonin/melatonin and the NAD+-precursor arms of tryptophan catabolism. A brief Limitations paragraph notes that FELLA RWR was unavailable and that the glycerophospholipid/pyrimidine hits for the two non-tryptophan metabolites are weak (p > 0.04) and should be interpreted with caution.

  "narrative_text": "Three independent pathway-analysis tools converge on a single dominant biological signal: tryptophan metabolism is the unambiguous top-ranked pathway in the differential metabolite set. RaMP multi-DB ORA reports KEGG:map00380 (Tryptophan metabolism) with an FDR of 8.86e-19 and a fold-enrichment of 875, hitting seven of the nine input metabolites. MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA reports hsa00380 (Tryptophan metabolism) at rank 0 with p = 5.41e-09, covering six input metabolites. Secondary pathway hits from RaMP (WP:WP465 Tryptophan metabolism, WP:WP4210 Tryptophan catabolism leading to NAD+ production, REACT:R-HSA-209931 Serotonin and melatonin biosynthesis) are all consistent refinements of the same metabolic module. MetaboAnalystR's second-ranked hsa00760 (Nicotinate and niacin metabolism, p = 0.073) contains only quinolinic acid and is not supported by other tools; it is not treated as a consensus winner. The driver metabolites are L-tryptophan (the upstream substrate), serotonin (the central neurotransmitter branch point), melatonin (the downstream neuroendocrine product), 3-hydroxyanthranilic acid and quinolinic acid (the kynurenine-side分支), and the two upstream intermediates tryptamine and indoleacetaldehyde. react_result.final_narrative_text: Three independent pathway-analysis tools converge on a single dominant biological signal: tryptophan metabolism is the unambiguous top-ranked pathway in the differential metabolite set. RaMP multi-DB ORA reports KEGG:map00380 (Tryptophan metabolism) with an FDR of 8.86e-19 and a fold-enrichment of 875, hitting seven of the nine input metabolites. MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA reports hsa00380 (Tryptophan metabolism) at rank 0 with p = 5.41e-09, covering six input metabolites. Mummichog m/z-direct analysis returns MUMM:tryptophan_metabolism at rank 0 (p = 8.4e-05) with a near-complete overlap of 13 of 14 pathway members. The cross-paradigm consensus is strong: every paradigm that succeeded places tryptophan metabolism at rank 1. Secondary pathway hits from RaMP (WP:WP465 Tryptophan metabolism, WP:WP4210 Tryptophan catabolism leading to NAD+ production, REACT:R-HSA-209931 Serotonin and melatonin biosynthesis) are all consistent refinements of the same metabolic module. MetaboAnalystR's second-ranked hsa00760 (Nicotinate and niacin metabolism, p = 0.073) contains only quinolinic acid and is not supported by other tools; it is not treated as a consensus winner. The driver metabolites are L-tryptophan (the upstream substrate), serotonin (the central neurotransmitter branch point), melatonin (the downstream neuroendocrine product), 3-hydroxyanthranilic acid and quinolinic acid (the kynurenine-side分支), and the two upstream intermediates tryptamine and indoleacetaldehyde. The biological interpretation is that the treatment condition strongly perturbs the tryptophan metabolic network, simultaneously affecting the serotonin/melatonin neuroendocrine axis and the kynurenine/NAD+ catabolic arm. O-Phosphoethanolamine and N-carbamoyl-L-aspartic acid (ureidosuccinic acid) are detected in the differential set but do not contribute to the consensus tryptophan hit; their pathway membership was not verified across tools. Limitations: two tools (FELLA random-walk, sspa ORA) were unavailable or failed, constraining the network-diffusion paradigm coverage; mummichog required re-calling with KEGG C-IDs to resolve metabolites, and query_pathway_members returned no results for KEGG/WP namespaces.

RaMP multi-DB ORA reports KEGG:map00380 (Tryptophan metabolism) with an FDR of 8.86e-19 and a fold-enrichment of 875, hitting seven of the nine input metabolites. final_react_result.final_narrative_text: Three independent pathway-analysis tools converge on a single dominant biological signal: tryptophan metabolism is the unambiguous top-ranked pathway in the differential metabolite set. RaMP multi-DB ORA reports KEGG:map00380 (Tryptophan metabolism) with an FDR of 8.86e-19 and a fold-enrichment of 875, hitting seven of the nine input metabolites. MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA reports hsa00380 (Tryptophan metabolism) at rank 0 with p = 5.41e-09, covering six input metabolites. Mummichog m/z-direct analysis returns MUMM:tryptophan_metabolism at rank 0 (p = 8.4e-05) with a near-complete overlap of 13 of 14 pathway members. The cross-paradigm consensus is strong: every paradigm that succeeded places tryptophan metabolism at rank 1. Secondary pathway hits from RaMP (WP:WP465 Tryptophan metabolism, WP:WP4210 Tryptophan catabolism leading to NAD+ production, REACT:R-HSA-209931 Serotonin and melatonin biosynthesis) are all consistent refinements of the same metabolic module. MetaboAnalystR's second-ranked hsa00760 (Nicotinate and niacin metabolism, p = 0.073) contains only quinolinic acid and is not supported by other tools; it is not treated as a consensus winner. The driver metabolites are L-tryptophan (the upstream substrate), serotonin (the central neurotransmitter branch point), melatonin (the downstream neuroendocrine product), 3-hydroxyanthranilic acid and quinolinic acid (the kynurenine-side分支), and the two upstream intermediates tryptamine and indoleacetaldehyde. The biological interpretation is that the treatment condition strongly perturbs the tryptophan metabolic network, simultaneously affecting the serotonin/melatonin neuroendocrine axis and the kynurenine/NAD+ catabolic arm. O-Phosphoethanolamine and N-carbamoyl-L-aspartic acid (ureidosuccinic acid) are detected in the differential set but do not contribute to the consensus tryptophan hit; their pathway membership was not verified across tools. Limitations: two tools (FELLA random-walk, sspa ORA) were unavailable or failed, constraining the network-diffusion paradigm coverage; mummichog required re-calling with KEGG C-IDs to resolve metabolites, and query_pathway_members returned no results for KEGG/WP namespaces.
